finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id deletes any project regardless of owner because the authorized() result is discarded, so any user can delete any other user's project.
finding.source: api.js:16 router.delete('/projects/:id') with req.params.id and req.user supplied by the caller

trace.note: project loaded by attacker-supplied id, no owner scoping in the query
authorized(req.user, project) evaluated but its boolean return is ignored

finding.guards_checked: authorized() at api.js:12-14 is a pure predicate with correct logic but unused result (ineffective). Sibling authorize() at api.js:4-10 throws on mismatch and is used correctly by PUT at api.js:25 (SAFE). No ownership scoping in the store lookup at api.js:17. Whether req.user is populated only for authenticated callers is UNCERTAIN because the mounting middleware is outside this repo.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean, but the call at api.js:18 is a bare statement whose result is discarded, so nothing aborts before the delete at api.js:19. The store lookup at api.js:17 has no owner scoping. The sibling authorize() at api.js:4-10 throws, but the DELETE route does not call it; it is only used by the PUT route at api.js:25.
verdict.reason: All trace lines match: api.js:16-20 loads the project by attacker-supplied id, discards the boolean from authorized() at api.js:18, deletes at api.js:19, and returns 204 at api.js:20. The attacker must be an authenticated low-privilege user, since an unpopulated req.user makes api.js:13 throw a TypeError before the delete; the only other repo file is api.js, so whether the outer middleware sets req.user is outside this repo and does not change the verdict for authenticated callers.
